newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soil moisture good in Brazil's key soybean regions.
newsitem.headline: Soil moisture good in Brazil's key soybean regions.

text.p: Conditions were favourable in Brazil's key soybean growing regions with good soil moisture and some rain over the weekend, cooperatives said.
"Rainfall has been above normal and things are looking good in terms of climate," said Nivaldo Sandri, agronomist at the Copacol cooperative in Cafelandia, Parana state.
Scattered showers fell in the region over the weekend and fresh rains were forecast for Jan 27 and 28, with temperatures currently ranging between 16 and 22 degrees Celsius, according to Sandri.
"It rained quite a lot, we got 70 mm over the weekend," said Ademar Dressler, agronomist at the Camp cooperative in Prudentopolis. "It is likely to continue raining today."
In Ijui in Rio Grande do Sul state, there was no rain over the weekend but it could arrive soon.
"We're still all right for another four to five days without rain," said Joao Henrich, agronomist at the Cotriba cooperative. "It's been raining 50 to 60 km from here and it looks like rain today."
Temperatures were forecast to rise to a maximum of 36 degrees C during the day, Henrich added.

In Mato Grosso state, some areas had already started harvesting, principally in the north. In the Diamantino region, half the crop was at the seed formation stage and 30 percent was in the flowering phase.
"We plan to start harvesting at the end of February," said Ernesto Pedrollo, agronomist at the Coopervale cooperative. "Soil moisture is good and it's cloudy -- it could rain any moment."
